classification: Current source-grounded research planning; supplementary prospective context, no historical benchmark features
availability_rule: Available at actual retrieval time; publication dates alone never backdate availability
publication: Links, metadata, authored summaries and hashes only; raw provider responses retained privately

sources.summary: NVIDIA describes supplier expansion across substrates, packaging, testing and optics, with additions scheduled into 2027–2028. These are plans rather than verified rentable GPU capacity.
sources.caveat: Do not convert announced manufacturing capacity into available GPU-hours or an automatic rental-price decline.

sources.summary: AWS and NVIDIA describe additional deployments across 2027–2028 and broader infrastructure collaboration. Delivery timing, location and realized utilization remain separate questions.
sources.caveat: A deployment announcement is not a transaction, current quote or capacity guarantee.

sources.summary: AWS announces P6-B300 availability in additional regions and describes its multi-GPU memory and networking configuration. It can motivate a substitution or regional-coverage hypothesis.
sources.caveat: An eight-GPU B300 instance cannot be equated with a per-GPU H100/A100 contract without verifying units and configuration.

sources.summary: Berkeley Lab documents generation and storage projects seeking grid interconnection and emphasizes withdrawals and long development timelines.
sources.caveat: Generation/storage queues are not data-center load queues or direct measures of GPU availability.

sources.summary: The Berkeley Lab update models data-center electricity consumption under alternative equipment, utilization and deployment assumptions. It supplies scenarios and measurement distinctions for long-run research.
sources.caveat: Annual energy consumption, peak power and interconnection requests are different quantities; these scenarios are not rental forecasts.

sources.summary: NVIDIA describes Rubin architecture and workload-specific efficiency claims. Those claims motivate checks on hardware substitution and workload economics.
sources.caveat: Vendor performance and cost-per-token claims do not establish GPU-hour rental prices.

forward_use: Separate exploratory market-context selector only; primary selector controls and archived studies unchanged
